column4: the bitmatrix v3 recipe refuses a test import of org.junit.jupiter.api and of com.sun.management (neither a java./javax./jdk. prefix nor a mapped package); declared EXTERNAL rows admit them, the probe's JDK module jdk.management is added to the test compile only (--add-modules jdk.management, --add-reads org.m3jdk.compression=jdk.management) so the product descriptor stays java.base only

column4: the format oracle reaches the encoders through method handles by class name, so one driver replays donor and relocated classes; its report carries no class name and no timing (timing goes to stderr), so the two reports compare byte for byte
column5: differential.sh (b): M3CompressionFormatOracle IDENTICAL

column4: a strict decoder that never rejects proves nothing: two one-line spec mutants (LZ4 LAST_LITERALS 5 -> 4, Snappy MAX_COPY_LENGTH 64 -> 65, which wraps the COPY_2 length field) shadow the relocated class on the class path and must be refused
column5: mutant lz4_last_literals REFUSED (LZ4 match reaches the last 5 bytes); mutant snappy_copy_length REFUSED (Snappy decoded size differs)

column4: every JVM (Maven, surefire, java) gets -Djava.io.tmpdir on the scratch drive: the Windows default temp is on a forbidden drive; surefire takes it through -DargLine, Maven through MAVEN_OPTS, the native lz4-java / snappy-java loaders of the scratch differential extract their libraries there
column5: verify.sh, differential.sh

column4: the chunk cache is format-neutral (java.util, java.security only) and independent of the encoders, so it is a second commit of the same module and recipe rather than a second PR: its three OMIT rows became FILE rows and relocate.py wrote exactly those three files (files=13 changed=3)
column5: relocate run 2: files=13 held=25 changed=3 provenance=CHANGED

column4: the cache is direct-mapped with a byte-budget LRU over occupied slots, not a plain LRU map: the reference model repeats only the owner's slot function (collisions are observable) and models contents (HashMap) and recency (access-ordered LinkedHashMap) independently; a hit touches, a fitting miss evicts the slot occupant then the eldest slots, an oversized miss changes nothing, trim keeps the counters
column5: M3CompressedChunkCacheModel: 200,000 operations, 1,399,108 field checks, 0 mismatches

column4: the donor cache's nested DeterministicEncoder is reached through java.lang.reflect.Proxy so the same driver replays the donor class by name; the proxy counts encoder calls, which must equal the model's misses one operation at a time
column5: differential.sh (e): M3CompressedChunkCacheModel IDENTICAL over donor and relocated caches

column4: the generalized mutant() shifts its five fixed arguments to pass oracle arguments through, so the label must be saved in a local first (the first run printed the oracle argument as the label and then failed on an unbound $1 under set -u)
column5: differential-2 run 1 exit 1; run 2 PASS with three mutants REFUSED

column4: the develop head moved (165ceb5a0202) after the pin, but the compression trees are identical (main 4f5f3e6a40e2, test c5bd75be1ffb), so the leaf keeps the pinned 6fdee5330b8a; the native crates newer than develop (jni-boundaries e31eada6, retained pr14828 fast paths 8c00db54) are unpromoted HOLD candidates by their own READMEs, so develop's c07a1e4f stays the native lineage
column5: git rev-parse <rev>:synexia-algo/src/{main,test}/java/com/synexia/algorithms/compression; crate manifests pre/post sha256

column4: decoders refuse with different messages for the same defect (the donor folds offset and length faults of a Snappy copy into one message, the reference splits them; the reference checks LZ4 end-of-block rules before an overrun): compare refusal classes, not messages, as class sets per message that must intersect, and fail on any message without a class so a new refusal path cannot pass unnoticed
column5: mutant lz4_decoder_offset_zero_check REFUSED: refusal message without a class

column4: the reference Snappy decoder has no output cap and would allocate a fuzzed declared length (up to 2^31 - 9 bytes); the fuzz lane pre-reads the varint and runs the reference only when the declared length is within the donor's cap (the donor must refuse the rest)
column5: FUZZ_SNAPPY_REFERENCE_NOT_RUN_DECLARED_PAST_CAP=46809; -Xmx256m run completes

column4: the encoders never emit Snappy COPY_1 / COPY_4 tags or non-minimal literal headers, so encoder streams alone leave decoder paths dead: grammar streams carry them, and the COPY_1 mutant is refused only by the grammar stage
column5: mutant snappy_decoder_copy1_length REFUSED: Snappy GRAMMAR round trip refused

column4: no encoder takes its index as a parameter and the classes of #2613 must stay byte-identical, so the four-way output comes from an encoder twin in test scope, which is first proven equal to both encoders over the direct-mapped index (100,000 inputs) before it is trusted over the four-way index
column5: TWIN_DIRECT_IDENTICAL=100000

column4: the Bash tool collapses doubled backslashes inside heredocs, so a Python edit carrying a doubled backslash (\r, \n, \& meant as two characters) in a shell script must come from a file written by the Write tool (the first splice of differential.sh turned tr -d '\r' into a raw carriage return)
column5: differential.sh splice from S:/m3-scratch/eb-conv/compress2/tools/diff_block.sh

column4: the donor C files start with a line-comment SPDX line and the bitmatrix-derived C path accepted only block comments; the extension accepts both (keeping the donor's comment style for the M3JDK header) and relocates CMakeLists.txt FILE rows with a # header and a #FLLDCIM anchor; the version stays v3 so the 26 earlier anchors do not churn, and --check stays a fixed point over all 35 rows
column5: first native run files=35 held=6 changed=9, then changed=0

column4: a C file compiled with -include of its own javac -h header turns any prototype drift into a compile error, and the exported Java_ symbols (nm -D) compared with the header's prototypes catch a missing or extra entry point; both pass for the relocated symbol prefix

column4: the WSL distribution disk lives on a forbidden drive (E:), so the native gate keeps every temporary file under its out-dir (TMPDIR, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS -XX:-UsePerfData and java.io.tmpdir) and the WSL Maven run sets HOME, TMPDIR and maven.repo.local on S:; with HOME moved, JAVA_HOME must be given explicitly (the first rerun found no JDK under the moved HOME and failed at jni.h)

column4: on this Windows host the default m3 reactor fails outside m3/compression for host reasons: exec-maven-plugin steps call python3, which resolves to the Microsoft Store stub (a scratch python3.cmd shim on PATH gets past it), m3/fs needs a C compiler for CMake, and the OpenRewrite 8.17.1-m3-source-1 artifacts of the recipe modules are not on Maven Central
